notes.summary: Verified the external analytic premises and reconstructed the canonical-removal, normalized L1, and smooth Gauduchon lemmas needed below.
notes.detailedSummary: The input's attained maximal-subsolution characterization remains an explicit grant. Public primary sources verify smooth Hermitian solvability, canonical representatives, removable singularities, non-pluripolar locality, and bounded Hermitian products. The auxiliary Gauduchon and normalized L1 arguments are reconstructed. Direct downloads failed, but the relevant primary PDFs were inspected through the web tool. No arbitrary-L1 finite-mass theorem is imported.
notes.text:
Status: ordinary unverified mathematical draft. Execution success does not certify mathematical correctness.

The input grants, for every smooth positive Hermitian background α, that b_α(f) is the attained largest coefficient in MA_ext_α(w)≥a f dV among genuine α-psh potentials, and equals lim_j c_α(min(f,j)). This grant is used explicitly rather than inferred from literature. For bounded f, truncation eventually becomes constant, hence b_α(f)=c_α(f). For arbitrary nonzero f, the coefficient is finite because b_α(f)≤c_α(min(f,1))<∞. No independent positivity assertion for every arbitrary L1 density is required below; the smooth-data coefficients are positive and finite.

Primary-source checks, conducted on 2026-10-07:

1. Tosatti–Weinkove, The complex Monge-Ampère equation on compact Hermitian manifolds, arXiv:0910.1390v2, Corollary 1, PDF page 1: https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.1390v2. For any compact Hermitian metric α and smooth strictly positive f, apply the theorem with F=log(f dV/α^n) and w=2πϕ. Its equation becomes (α+dd^c w)^n=c f dV with α+dd^c w>0 and w smooth. The scalar is c_α(f), since this is a bounded continuous solution of the input's scalar equation. The theorem requires neither closedness nor a positive lower Monge-Ampère volume. Its nonlinear PDE proof is an external premise, verified at the primary statement; it is not claimed to be re-proved here.

2. Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, author's public manuscript: https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf. Chapter I, Theorems 5.7, 5.8 and 5.24, PDF pages 39–40 and 45, provide upper envelopes, unique canonical psh representatives of distributions with positive complex Hessian, and extension across closed pluripolar sets under local upper bounds. Proposition 4.21, PDF page 36, supplies local L1 precompactness. Chapter III, equation 2.15, PDF page 143, verifies Poincaré–Lelong. These are local facts without a global Kähler hypothesis. The normalization conversion gives dd^c log|g|²=[div(g)] for the input's dd^c.

3. Gauduchon, Les métriques standard d'une surface complexe compacte à premier nombre de Betti pair, Astérisque 126 (1985), pages 129–135: https://numdam.org/item/AST_1985__126__129_0.pdf. Despite the title, Section 3, Theorem 2 and its proof on printed page 132 concern conformal standard metrics in every dimension greater than one. Section 1 identifies the integrable condition as dd^c(ω^(n−1))=0. The original-author proof was checked, including strict positivity of the adjoint-kernel generator.

4. Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi, Monge-Ampère equations in big cohomology classes, arXiv:0812.3674v2: https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2. Section 1.2, Definition 1.1 and Proposition 1.4, PDF pages 5–6, verify local non-pluripolar construction, locality, dependence on the positive currents, and absence of mass on pluripolar sets. The discussion before Theorem 1.11 allows locally infinite positive Borel measures. Only these local properties, combined with the input's smooth-background corrections, are applied to nonclosed backgrounds. Global Kähler finiteness is not imported.

5. Guedj–Lu, Quasi-plurisubharmonic envelopes 2: Bounds on Monge-Ampère volumes, arXiv:2106.04272: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2106.04272. Section 1.1.1, PDF pages 4–5, constructs bounded Hermitian products using local closed-background corrections and verifies their positivity and independence of the chosen background. It supports the bounded product and Stokes calculations below, not a finite-mass assertion for arbitrary unbounded potentials.

Canonical recovery and removal. If an L1 distribution w satisfies dd^c w≥−α for a smooth form α, locally choose a smooth ρ with dd^cρ≥α. The distribution w+ρ has a unique genuine psh representative. These representatives patch by uniqueness, giving a canonical quasi-psh representative of w. Consequently genuine quasi-psh functions agreeing almost everywhere agree everywhere.

If w is α-psh off an analytic hypersurface D and locally bounded above near D, extend w+ρ by the psh removable-extension theorem. Positivity of α+dd^c w survives removal even when α is nonclosed: write it as S+(α−dd^cρ), with S=dd^c(w+ρ) a positive order-zero current. Off D positivity is already known. On D the smooth correction has zero measure, leaving the positive restriction of S. This proves positivity everywhere.

Uniform normalized L1 bound. For fixed positive α on connected compact X, there is K such that sup_X w=0 and w∈PSH(X,α) imply ∫|w|dV≤K. Otherwise choose w_j≤0 with sup w_j=0 and B_j=−∫w_j dV→∞. Put v_j=w_j/B_j. They have L1 norm 1 and dd^c v_j≥−α/B_j. Local addition of ρ/B_j gives locally L1-bounded psh functions, so a finite-chart diagonal subsequence converges in L1(X). The limit has dd^c v≥0 globally, hence is constant on compact connected X; its integral is −1, so v=−1. Submean on fixed-radius balls applied to v_j+ρ/B_j bounds v_j uniformly above by −1+o(1) on smaller charts. A finite cover contradicts sup v_j=0. This establishes the bound for canonical representatives.

Smooth Gauduchon construction. For a smooth positive B define Lψ=(dd^cψ∧B^(n−1))/B^n. It is real uniformly elliptic with no zero-order term. The maximum principle gives ker L equal to the constants. Its Fredholm index is zero, by deformation to a Laplacian, so ker L* is one-dimensional and has a smooth generator σ. A nonzero nonnegative function cannot lie in im L. If σ changed sign, a smooth strictly positive function orthogonal to σ would lie in im L by the Fredholm alternative, a contradiction. Orient σ nonnegative. The local strong maximum principle, with the usual local conjugation handling a bounded zero-order term, makes σ strictly positive. Integration by parts yields dd^c(σ B^(n−1))=0. Normalize by Z=∫h∧σ B^(n−1)>0 to obtain the genuine smooth test T=σ B^(n−1)/Z used below. No singular test is involved.

Artifacts and evidence: input.json contains the supplied input. web_source_evidence.json records browsing outputs. The runtime policy snapshot allowed HTTP, but the local socket restriction prevailed; no bypass was attempted. No supervised mathematical compute service was exposed, and no resource-heavy computation was needed or launched. No author-specific S12 article, private proof, other campaign files, or credentials were consulted.

notes.summary: A is proved for the entire one-sided class: canonical divisor subtraction gives a bijection with PSH(X,h−β_E), preserves extended MA, and attains b_(h−β_E)(f).
notes.detailedSummary: With h_E>0, ordinary order u≼ℓ_E, the representation u=ℓ_E+w with genuine h_E-psh w, and actual domination h+dd^c u≥[E] describe the same class. Removal and canonical uniqueness establish equality at every point. Extended non-pluripolar measures agree even without finite mass. Ordinary equivalence corresponds exactly to bounded residuals. Arbitrary-L1 attainment is proved only in the full one-sided class.
notes.text:
Target A. Write D=supp(E), ℓ=ℓ_E and α=h−β_E>0. Define
B_≤(f;ℓ)=sup{a≥0: genuine u∈PSH(X,h), u≼ℓ, MA_ext_h(u)≥a f dV}.
The reference is the ordinary singularity type of ℓ. Neither finite mass nor an exact equation is an admissibility requirement.

There is a canonical bijection
PSH(X,α) → {u∈PSH(X,h):u≼ℓ},  w↦ℓ+w.
This class also equals {u∈PSH(X,h):h+dd^c u≥[E]}.

For the forward direction, every genuine w on compact X has a finite upper bound, so ℓ+w≼ℓ. Its genuine quasi-psh sum satisfies
h+dd^c(ℓ+w)=[E]+α+dd^c w≥[E].
At every point of D, ℓ+w=−∞ canonically.

Conversely, suppose u≤ℓ+C. Off D put w=u−ℓ. There ℓ is smooth, α+dd^c w=h+dd^c u≥0, and w≤C. The removal lemma in n1 extends w as a genuine α-psh potential, including positivity for the nonclosed background. The genuine functions u and ℓ+w have the same L1 distribution on X; canonical uniqueness makes them equal everywhere. This proves both surjectivity and domination by [E]. Residual uniqueness follows in the same way.

If instead actual domination h+dd^c u≥[E] is given, form w=u−ℓ as an L1 distribution, never by subtracting infinite values on D. It satisfies α+dd^c w=h+dd^c u−[E]≥0. Canonical recovery gives a genuine residual, equality u=ℓ+w everywhere, and hence u≼ℓ. Thus domination is characterized as an actual current inequality, not a cohomological pairing.

The measure identity is
MA_ext_h(ℓ+w)=MA_ext_α(w).
On X\D the total currents agree, so the extended products agree by locality and the smooth-background correction identity. Both measures give D zero mass because D is pluripolar; hence equality holds globally, including potentially infinite measures. Equivalently, intersect the plurifine loci where u and w are bounded, apply the bounded-product smooth-shift identity there, and exhaust X\D. This avoids any subtraction of infinite quantities.

Every coefficient inequality therefore transports in both directions. The input's attained maximal-subsolution characterization for α proves
B_≤(f;ℓ)=b_α(f).
If w_* is its genuine attaining subsolution, u_*=ℓ+w_* genuinely attains the one-sided maximum. This proves A for every nonzero f≥0 in L1(dV). No boundedness, ordinary equivalence, finite mass, exact equation, or stretching membership is asserted for that general-L1 attainer.

Additionally, u~ℓ exactly when its residual w is bounded. The two ordinary inequalities bound w off D; its removable canonical extension retains both bounds. Conversely bounded w supplies the two inequalities everywhere, with the prescribed canonical pole interpretation.

For E=0 the correspondence is the identity, and u≼0 is the entire genuine h-psh class. The global threshold can differ from the restricted one, as explicitly demonstrated in n4 and n6.

This proof neither equates all Gauduchon currents with smooth-test limits nor defines [E]∧T for singular T. Artifact: proofs.txt and notes.json, regenerated by `python3 build_notes.py`.

notes.summary: B is proved canonically: P_h[ℓ_E]~ℓ_E, and every ordinary-equivalent potential belongs to the exact stretching class through explicit witnesses.
notes.detailedSummary: A uniform residual bound for all envelope competitors prevents usc regularization from filling divisor poles. Choquet approximation and canonical recovery establish genuineness for nonclosed h. For u≥ℓ_E−A and φ_E≤ℓ_E+B, the witnesses a_t=ℓ_E−tA−(t−1)B establish every stretching inequality. No replacement by envelope equality is made. General-L1 thresholds in the narrower classes are only bounded, without an attainment claim.
notes.text:
Target B. The family defining φ=P_h[ℓ] consists of genuine h-psh v≤0 with v≼ℓ. It contains ℓ because sup ℓ=0 and h+dd^cℓ=α+[E]≥0.

By n2 every competitor is canonically ℓ+w with w∈PSH(X,α). Choose a relatively compact nonempty U⊂X\D and M with −ℓ≤M on U. The obstacle gives w≤M there. Put s=sup_X w. The normalized L1 bound of n1 implies
−K≤∫_U(w−s)dV≤(M−s)vol_dV(U),
so s≤M+K/vol_dV(U)=B, increasing B to be nonnegative. This bound is uniform over all competitors, although their individual ordinary-order constants need not initially be uniform. Consequently
ℓ≤φ≤ℓ+B.
Upper regularization preserves the upper bound because ℓ+B is usc. Thus φ=−∞ at every point of D; divisor poles are not filled in.

Genuineness requires preserving the original lower Hessian bound. Choose a countable Choquet subfamily with the same usc supremum and include ℓ. Finite maxima of h-psh functions remain h-psh: on a relatively compact coordinate chart, convolution gives smooth Hessians bounded below by −h−εω. A smooth convex maximum has Hessian at least the weighted average of these Hessians plus a positive gradient term. Passing to the ordinary maximum and then to the L1 limit preserves the bound −h. After adding a smooth dominating local potential, the psh maximum property identifies the distribution with its genuine pointwise maximum.

The increasing finite maxima lie between ℓ and 0, hence converge in L1_loc. Positivity of h+dd^c passes to the limit. The local upper-envelope theorem identifies the canonical representative with the usc envelope defining φ. Therefore φ is genuine and ordinarily equivalent to ℓ. Its residual q=φ−ℓ, extended canonically as in n2, is bounded with 0≤q≤B.

For u~ℓ choose A≥0 with u≥ℓ−A. For every real t≥1 set
a_t=ℓ−tA−(t−1)B.
This is a genuine h-psh potential. Off D,
t^−1 a_t+(1−t^−1)φ≤ℓ−A≤u.
For t>1 the left side is canonically −∞ on D, so the inequality holds there as well. At t=1 use a_1≤u directly, without evaluating zero times −∞. Also u≼φ because φ~ℓ. These are precisely the original stretching definition's conditions. Hence
{u:u~ℓ}⊂E_env(X,h,φ)⊂{u:u≼ℓ}.
The second inclusion follows from the defining order restriction and φ~ℓ. No stretching/envelope-equality equivalence is assumed.

For arbitrary L1 data define B_ord(f;ℓ) and B_env(f;φ) as suprema of the same coefficient inequalities over these exact classes. The proved characterization yields
0≤B_ord(f;ℓ)≤B_env(f;φ)≤b_α(f).
The ordinary class corresponds to all bounded genuine residuals. Neither equality with b_α(f) nor attainment of either narrower supremum is asserted for general L1 data. Target C supplies both for smooth strictly positive f. For E=0, φ=0 and the witnesses establish stretching membership of every bounded h-psh potential.

notes.summary: C is proved: all three prescribed classes have the attained smooth-data maximum c_(h−β_E)(f), strictly below c_h(f) for E>0 without nefness or semipositivity.
notes.detailedSummary: The smooth residual equation produces an ordinary-equivalent genuine solution with exact finite extended equation and the asserted mass. A gives the upper bound and B proves stretching membership. A smooth Gauduchon form calibrated to the global smooth solution gives c_(h−β_E)(f)≤c_h(f)(1−I)^n, where I=∫_[E]T lies strictly between zero and one. Divisor pairing is legitimate because T is smooth.
notes.text:
Target C. Let f be smooth strictly positive and α=h−β_E>0. The primary smooth Hermitian theorem checked in n1 gives smooth w with
A=α+dd^c w>0,  A^n=c_α(f) f dV.
The genuine u=ℓ_E+w is ordinarily equivalent to ℓ_E. By n2,
MA_ext_h(u)=c_α(f) f dV,
with total mass c_α(f)∫f dV, finite and positive. Its actual current is [E]+A. By n3 it belongs to the exact stretching class relative to φ_E=P_h[ℓ_E].

Since bounded f has b_α(f)=c_α(f), A bounds every one-sided competitor by this coefficient. The class inclusions in B and the explicit u show that the ordinary, one-sided, and stretching suprema are all attained maxima equal to c_α(f).

For strict comparison when E>0, let v be the global smooth solution and put
B=h+dd^c v>0,  B^n=c_h(f) f dV.
Use n1 to construct T=σ B^(n−1)/Z, with σ>0, dd^c T=0 and ∫h∧T=1. Diagonalizing A relative to B gives the elementary arithmetic-geometric mean inequality
A∧B^(n−1)≥(A^n/B^n)^(1/n)B^n.
Here A^n/B^n=c_α(f)/c_h(f) is constant. Multiply by σ/Z and integrate. Since ∫B∧T=1,
∫A∧T≥(c_α(f)/c_h(f))^(1/n).
On the other hand integration by parts gives
∫A∧T=1−I,  I=∫β_E∧T=∫_[E]T.
The last equality uses the distribution dd^cℓ_E against a smooth dd^c-closed test. It does not define a divisor product with a singular current. Since E is nonzero effective and T smooth strictly positive, I>0. Since A>0, 1−I>0. Therefore
0<c_α(f)≤c_h(f)(1−I)^n<c_h(f)=b_h(f).
No sign condition on β_E and no nefness is used.

A concrete positive finite gap is X=P^n, h=ω_FS normalized by ∫h^n=1, dV=h^n, f=1, and E=λ times a hyperplane with 0<λ<1 and β_E=λh. The residual zero potential solves the equation, so the global threshold is 1 and every prescribed maximum is (1−λ)^n. This establishes that the global coefficient need not equal the restricted one.

notes.summary: D is proved: every global threshold subsolution for smooth strictly positive data has no actual nonzero effective real divisorial component.
notes.detailedSummary: Scale a hypothetical dominated divisor by δ>0 until h−δβ_E is positive. Canonical subtraction gives a residual potential and places u in the corresponding entire one-sided class. A bounds its coefficient by c_(h−δβ_E)(f), while C makes that coefficient strictly smaller than b_h(f). No residual positivity for the original divisor, finite mass, uniform integrability, or singular-current pairing is needed. Original S12 closure remains false.
notes.text:
Target D. Suppose a genuine threshold subsolution satisfies MA_ext_h(u)≥b_h(f) f dV for smooth strictly positive f, and suppose h+dd^c u≥[E] for a nonzero effective real divisor E.

Choose a smooth closed β_E and canonical ℓ_E. Compactness and smoothness permit δ∈(0,1] sufficiently small that α_δ=h−δβ_E>0. This imposes no positivity condition on h−β_E.

The L1 distribution w=u−δℓ_E satisfies
α_δ+dd^c w=h+dd^c u−δ[E]≥0.
Canonical recovery from n1 gives a genuine residual and the identity u=δℓ_E+w everywhere. Thus u≼δℓ_E, including canonical pole values.

A applied to δE bounds the coefficient of u by
b_h(f)≤b_αδ(f)=c_αδ(f).
C applied to the same nonzero δE gives
c_αδ(f)<c_h(f)=b_h(f),
a contradiction. Therefore actual nonzero effective divisorial domination is impossible.

The singular u can have excess or infinite extended mass; n2 transports its inequality without a finite-mass premise. The argument does not infer domination from cohomological pairings, identify singular currents with smooth-test limits, or define [E]∧T for singular T. It requires no nefness, semipositive representative, or uniform-integrability hypothesis.

This establishes a smooth-data obstruction. It supplies no sufficient inverse realization condition for general L1 densities. Original S12 closure=false.

notes.summary: E is proved with κ equal to the Fubini–Study form determined by its logarithm, including exact restricted thresholds, stretching, and conditional zero lower volumes with nonclosed backgrounds.
notes.detailedSummary: For the standard normalized Fubini–Study form, block degrees give H^N=CV0μ and H_E^N=CV0(1−λ)^kμ. Zero residual potentials compute the coefficients, while u=λℓ supplies the genuine divisor and finite equation. Pullbacks of bounded factor potentials prove both lower-volume infima vanish when v_-(h0)=0. Bounded Kähler Stokes makes that hypothesis incompatible with closed h0, forcing both backgrounds nonclosed. No example of a zero-volume factor is imported. Normalization alone does not specify this κ; n7 addresses the literal limitation.
notes.text:
Target E with its standard-projective-metric specification made explicit. Set κ=ω_FS, determined in homogeneous local trivializations by dd^c log(Σ|Z_i|²), with ∫_Yκ^k=1. Then for the displayed genuine logarithm,
dd^cℓ=[D]−κ,  sup ℓ=0.
All factor forms below are pulled back to X=X0×Y. Write N=m+k, C=binomial(N,m), V0=∫h0^m>0, and
H=h0+κ,  H_E=h0+(1−λ)κ>0,
μ=(h0^m/V0)∧κ^k,  R=μ/dV.
For every smooth positive probability dV, R is smooth strictly positive and ∫R dV=1.

Exactly one binomial term survives in top degree: the h0 exponent cannot exceed m, and the κ exponent cannot exceed k. Hence
H^N=C h0^m∧κ^k=CV0 R dV,
H_E^N=C(1−λ)^k h0^m∧κ^k=CV0(1−λ)^k R dV.
Zero potentials are smooth normalized positive solutions. Scalar uniqueness and bounded-data truncation give
b_H(R)=c_H(R)=CV0,
b_H_E(R)=c_H_E(R)=CV0(1−λ)^k.
A–C therefore identify all three prescribed maxima with the latter coefficient.

Directly, u=λℓ is genuine and satisfies
H+dd^c u=H_E+λ[D]≥λ[D],
MA_ext_H(u)=H_E^N=CV0(1−λ)^k R dV.
Its total mass is CV0(1−λ)^k. It is ordinarily equivalent to the reference, and n3 gives genuine stretching membership relative to P_H[λℓ]. Since 0<λ<1, this positive finite prescribed threshold is strictly below the global one. The example does not realize a divisor at the global threshold.

Assume now v_-(h0)=0. Choose bounded genuine h0-psh w_j with M_j=∫(h0+dd^c w_j)^m→0. Their pullbacks W_j are bounded genuine H-psh and H_E-psh. The bounded Hermitian product construction and block degrees give
∫(H+dd^c W_j)^N=C M_j,
∫(H_E+dd^c W_j)^N=C(1−λ)^k M_j.
Nonnegativity of all admissible masses proves v_-(H)=v_-(H_E)=0.

If dh0=0, then h0 is Kähler. For bounded h0-psh w, the Bedford–Taylor recursive definition gives the current identity
(h0+dd^c w)^m−h0^m
=dd^c(w Σ_(r=0)^(m−1)(h0+dd^c w)^r∧h0^(m−1−r)).
Every factor in the sum is closed. Stokes yields the constant mass V0>0, contradicting v_-(h0)=0. Thus dh0≠0. Since κ is closed,
dH=dH_E=π0*dh0≠0;
this pullback is injective by restriction to x↦(x,y) at a fixed y. Both backgrounds are nonclosed.

For m=1 the hypothesis is impossible because every positive (1,1) form is closed. If zero-dimensional factors are allowed, h0^0=1, V0 is the number of points, and v_-(h0)=V0>0, so the conditional assertion is again vacuous. No named factor or existence theorem for v_-(h0)=0 is imported.

If arbitrary X0 includes disconnected compact manifolds, there are finitely many components. The displayed zero solutions have the same scalar on each component with V0 the total volume. Componentwise coefficient bounds, simultaneous normalization of dV and density, and finite-component envelope bounds give the same conclusions. The original connected-X convention restricts the example to connected X0.

Evidence: `python3 check_formulas.py > formula_checks.log` generates formula_checks.json. It checks exactly 56 finite cases, 1≤m≤8 and 2≤k≤8, finding the unique surviving exponent r=m and coefficient binomial(m+k,m). This is an exhaustive finite algebra check only. The block-degree argument above proves the all-dimension identity. No numerical PDE or computation of v_- is claimed. proofs.txt and notes.json are regenerated by `python3 build_notes.py`.

notes.summary: E needs an explicit Fubini–Study specification: volume normalization alone permits a counterexample to its claimed attainer. A–D are proved; original S12 remains unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: A small exact perturbation κ=ω_FS+dd^cψ retains normalized volume and positive residual but makes u=λℓ fail both the asserted equation and threshold inequality. At a point with dd^cψ=εω_FS, its density ratio exceeds (1−λ)^k. The corrected attainer is λℓ−λψ. Thus E is proved under the standard Fubini–Study interpretation and rejected under the normalization-only reading. Earlier primary results already contain the smooth residual equation, closed-case prescribed-type existence, and divisor deletion, with their application limits recorded. Candidate is false because all targets as written are not unconditionally certified.
notes.text:
The written E specifies ∫κ^k=1 but does not explicitly state that κ is the Fubini–Study form determined by its displayed logarithm. That logarithm always satisfies dd^cℓ=[D]−ω_FS. Volume normalization does not force κ=ω_FS. Therefore E is false under the interpretation allowing any normalized Kähler κ. Note n6 proves every assertion under the customary Fubini–Study interpretation. A clarification was requested during the work; no clarification is used as a premise here.

Counterexample under normalization alone. Take X0=P^1 with h0=ω1 and ∫h0=1, so m=1 and V0=1. Take k=2, or any k≥2, and 0<λ<1. Choose an affine chart of P^k away from D, centered at y0, and a smooth cutoff χ supported there and equal to one near y0. In standard coordinates set
ψ=εχΣ|z_i|²,
extended by zero. Then dd^cψ(y0)=εω_FS(y0). For every sufficiently small ε>0, compactness and the fixed cutoff's Hessian bound ensure
κ=ω_FS+dd^cψ>0,
η=κ−λω_FS=(1−λ)ω_FS+dd^cψ>0.
Stokes gives ∫κ^k=1 exactly. Set dV=μ=h0∧κ^k, a smooth positive probability measure, so R=1. Let E=λD, β_E=λω_FS, ℓ_E=λℓ and H=h0+κ. Even the positive-residual hypothesis holds: H−β_E=h0+η>0.

For the claimed explicit attainer u=λℓ,
H+dd^c u=h0+η+λ[D],
MA_ext_H(u)=C h0∧η^k,  C=k+1.
At y0 its density relative to Cμ is
η^k/κ^k=((1+ε−λ)/(1+ε))^k>(1−λ)^k.
The strict inequality persists on an open neighborhood. Thus the claimed equation fails as an actual measure equality.

Its total mass nevertheless equals C(1−λ)^k, since η is cohomologous to (1−λ)ω_FS. The prescribed threshold is exactly that coefficient: the smooth residual w=−λψ gives
H_E+dd^c w=h0+(1−λ)κ
and its top power is C(1−λ)^kμ; n4 provides the maximality. Since u's measure has the same total mass but differs from this density, it cannot dominate the threshold density. Hence u=λℓ is not even a threshold subsolution in this example. A corrected attainer is λℓ−λψ, up to a constant, or one can change the logarithmic reference to match κ. Neither correction may be made silently to E.

The rational diagnostic in formula_checks.log is 36/121>1/4, difference 23/484, for k=2, λ=1/2 and local ε=1/10. It illustrates the discrepancy only; global positivity of a particular cutoff at that numerical ε is not asserted. The proof works for every sufficiently small positive ε.

Earlier results and application limits. Tosatti–Weinkove's 2009/2010 Corollary 1 already contains the smooth residual equation used in C; canonical divisor subtraction transfers it to the ordinary class. BEGZ Section 3.1 explicitly adds an effective real divisor to a residual current and removes its contribution from the non-pluripolar equation. Its Theorem 3.1 supplies closed Kähler residual full-mass existence for non-pluripolar measures. Those statements do not supply nonclosed finite-mass solutions for arbitrary L1 data.
